
### mapping of sets to memory (direct-mapped) 



::: {.r-stack .my-full}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/setMappingDiagDM.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-out fragment-index=0 fig-alt="We draw the cache as a rectangle, width equal to block size, height equal to number of sets. Similarly, we draw the memory as a much taller rectangle, width equal to block size. If we mark set 0 and set K in the cache and mark the blocks of memory corresponding to set 0 and set K, the marks in memory form a repeating pattern as if we tiled the cache markings over the memory."}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/setMappingDiagDM.figure-2.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=1 fig-alt="Values which be stored in the same set in memory are [cache size]-bytes apart."}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/setMappingDiagDM.figure-3.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=2 fig-alt="If array[0] maps to cache set 0, then the first part of the array that is in cache set K will be array[X] where X = K * (array elements per cache block)"}

![](/caching-assoc/texfig/setMappingDiagDM.figure-4.svg){.fragment .fade-in-then-out fragment-index=3 fig-alt="If array[0] maps to cache set 0, then array[X] where X = cache size / array element size will map to cache set 0 also. In general, we need to worry about cache misses when array elements are around cache size bytes apart (or a multiple of the cache size)." }



:::
